extracted.intended_audience: general public, students, researchers, activists, and policymakers interested in social movements and sexual-harassment policy
extracted.subtask_description: A comprehensive Wikipedia-style article describing the origins, purpose, spread, impact, criticisms, policy proposals, and sectoral effects of the #MeToo movement. It summarizes debates, reforms, and examples across society and institutions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Empowerment through empathy
rubrics_metrics.description: The original purpose (Tarana Burke, 2006) was to empower women through empathy—affirming survivors they are not alone.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used as a guiding principle for organizing and outreach; encourages sharing experiences to build solidarity and reduce shame.

rubrics_metrics.name: Awareness by demonstrating prevalence
rubrics_metrics.description: Use of the phrase/hashtag to demonstrate the magnitude of sexual harassment and assault by visibly showing how many people have experienced it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Social-media campaigns (e.g., Milano's 2017 tweet) function as an awareness metric to reveal prevalence and spur public discussion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Support survivors while ensuring due process
rubrics_metrics.description: Balance measures that support survivors (e.g., believing and empowering them) with safeguards for due process for the accused.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Debate over false accusations vs. supporting victims; studies cited estimate false reports at 2–10%, and commentators urge preserving fairness while addressing rarity of false claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Process all untested rape kits
rubrics_metrics.description: A policy goal to ensure law-enforcement evidence is examined: process all untested rape kits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Listed among Burke's suggested goals to improve criminal-investigation responses and justice for survivors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Re-examine and update school policies
rubrics_metrics.description: Review and reform local school policies to better address sexual misconduct and to improve reporting and response mechanisms in educational settings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Linked to K–12 initiatives (MeTooK12) and Title IX training; highlights underreporting and need for better institutional policies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Improve vetting of teachers and school staff
rubrics_metrics.description: Stronger screening of educators and staff to prevent hiring individuals who pose risks to students.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Part of reforms recommended alongside background checks and fingerprinting for those who work with children.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fingerprinting and background checks for professionals working with children
rubrics_metrics.description: Require fingerprinting and background checks before professionals who work with children are cleared to start work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Presented as a concrete safety measure advocated by movement leaders to protect minors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sex education that teaches reporting and consent
rubrics_metrics.description: Implement sex education programs that teach children to report predatory behavior immediately and the basics of consent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Framed as prevention and early-intervention policy; suggested to reduce normalization of abusive behavior and clarify consent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Remove procedural barriers to filing complaints (e.g., cooling-off periods)
rubrics_metrics.description: Legislative/procedural reforms to remove requirements (such as months-long cooling-off) that delay the filing of complaints (e.g., the cited #MeToo bill for congressional staffers).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Intended to make complaint processes more accessible and timely for victims in institutional contexts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ban or limit pre-employment NDAs and hiding of cover-up payments
rubrics_metrics.description: Prohibit employers from requiring nondisclosure agreements as a condition of employment and restrict mechanisms that hide settlement/cover-up payments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Advocated to prevent silencing of victims and to increase corporate transparency for shareholders and the public.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibit mandatory arbitration for harassment disputes / allow access to courts
rubrics_metrics.description: Discourage or legislate against forcing employees into arbitration for sexual-harassment claims instead of permitting access to legal proceedings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Suggested as a reform to ensure fair adjudication and public accountability rather than private settlement mechanisms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Address workplace power imbalances via labor reforms
rubrics_metrics.description: Treat sexual harassment as a labor issue by removing economic barriers to reporting (examples include raising tipped minimum wages).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposes structural economic changes that reduce vulnerability and dependency which can enable harassment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Portable panic buttons and sector-specific safety tools
rubrics_metrics.description: Adopt tools like 'portable panic buttons' for vulnerable workers (e.g., hotel employees) as mandated safety measures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cited as an innovation (Seattle mandate example) to provide immediate worker protection and reduce abuse risk.

rubrics_metrics.name: Managerial oversight and internal accountability mechanisms
rubrics_metrics.description: Increase managerial oversight, create clear internal reporting mechanisms, and adopt proactive disciplinary measures to address harassment within organizations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes creating a culture that encourages employees to be open about serious problems and ensuring responses are effective and timely.

rubrics_metrics.name: Financial and regulatory penalties for companies that retain harassers
rubrics_metrics.description: Impose fines, remove tax breaks, or other financial penalties on companies that allow known harassers to remain employed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Suggested as a deterrent and accountability mechanism to change employer behavior.

rubrics_metrics.name: Strengthen labor unions and third-party reporting options
rubrics_metrics.description: Empower unions and external hotlines so workers can report harassment to bodies other than their employer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposed to reduce fear of employer retaliation and to trigger independent investigations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Industry hotlines and third-party investigation triggers
rubrics_metrics.description: Maintain sector-specific hotlines that have the power to initiate independent investigations into allegations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Seen as a way to bypass conflicted internal processes and provide neutral fact-finding when necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Digital reporting tools and victim-connection apps
rubrics_metrics.description: Develop and use apps that allow victims to report misconduct and to find others who have reported the same person.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These tools can facilitate corroboration and collective action but raise privacy and verification issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Verify whisper networks and balance privacy vs. public disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: When whisper networks (private lists of people to avoid) are used or leaked, establish verification mechanisms to ensure fairness and avoid weaponization.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Acknowledges defenders' view that whisper networks can protect vulnerable people while critics warn of unverified gossip being harmful; verification and fairness mechanisms are recommended.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bystander intervention and male ally engagement
rubrics_metrics.description: Encourage men to call out bad behavior, engage in discussions about consent, reflect on past conduct, and listen to survivors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Seen as a cultural strategy to reduce incidents and shift norms; includes campaigns like #HowIWillChange and calls for active male participation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presumptive credibility for less powerful accusers (cultural shift)
rubrics_metrics.description: Cultural change toward giving presumptive credibility to less powerful accusers because of the risks of going public and power differentials.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Framed as a societal shift in perceptions, not a legal standard; commentators note tensions with due process and speed of demanded change.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mandatory Title IX and K–12 training for education staff
rubrics_metrics.description: Require comprehensive training for education personnel about reporting sexual misconduct and how to respond under Title IX frameworks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cited because K–12 sexual misconduct is widely underreported; only some states currently mandate such training.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sanctions on funders/institutions for harassment (e.g., cut funding)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use funding consequences (such as NIH funding cuts) for individuals or groups found guilty of harassment as a disciplinary lever.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Offered as a policy tool particularly in academia and research (MeTooSTEM example).

rubrics_metrics.name: Reputational consequences (remove names/titles after substantiated abuse)
rubrics_metrics.description: Remove honors, building names, titles, and positions associated with individuals found to have committed harassment or abuse.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples include UC Irvine removing Francisco Ayala's name after substantiated allegations; used to signal institutional condemnation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transparency and diversity disclosures in industries
rubrics_metrics.description: Pressure firms (e.g., in finance) to disclose workforce diversity statistics and investigate industry culture.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Intended to spotlight structural inequalities and prompt accountability where harassment is prevalent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinguish legal, workplace, and private-intimate behaviors in responses
rubrics_metrics.description: Be clear about what behavior is criminal, what is legal but intolerable in the workplace, and what private intimate behavior is outside workplace policy scope.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Urges 'preserving the nuances' so responses are proportionate and appropriate across contexts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusivity: center marginalized survivors and expand movement reach
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure the movement includes marginalized groups (women of color, sex workers, incarcerated women, etc.) and addresses police abuse and institutional blind spots.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Critiques note #MeToo’s gaps in reach; calls emphasize centering those who face highest rates of violence and systemic barriers to reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Anti-retaliation protections for complainants
rubrics_metrics.description: Establish protocols and legal protections that prevent retaliation against those who file complaints about sexual harassment and assault.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Seen as essential to encourage reporting and protect victims from employer or community backlash.
